answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to compute and post a unique ridge of a high-dimensional spiral cost landscape whose parameters are set by a public comet-hash derived from recent random beacons. Generating a distinct valid ridge for a new identity demands fresh gradient descent runs that cannot be shared or precomputed, costing an attacker roughly 30-60 minutes of dedicated GPU time plus the opportunity cost of not using that hardware for productive work, while honest agents amortize the same computation across their real tasks.
